channel.itunes:author: Matthew S. Yorek
channel.itunes:summary: Deep Dive Audio Series • Moralizing Gods, Collective Ritual Synchrony, Sacred Institutions & Cultural Evolution

item.title: Which God Do You Turn To When Food Might Run Short? — Cross-Cultural Food-Worry Horizons, Moralistic vs. Local Deities & Christchurch Earthquake Panels
item.description: Statistical and anthropological evaluation of material insecurity and religious commitment (Baimel et al. 2022 across 14 populations; Purzycki et al. 2018; Sibley & Bulbulia 2012 Canterbury earthquake longitudinal panel).

item.title: Can a God Be Fooled? — Developmental False-Belief Tasks, Barrett's Cracker Box, Yukatek Maya Interviews & Omniscience vs. Moral Policing
item.description: Developmental cognitive science of supernatural minds: unexpected-contents false-belief tasks (Barrett et al. 2001; Knight et al. Yukatek Maya; Lane et al. preparedness vs. anthropomorphism) and separating epistemic omniscience from moral policing across development.

item.title: The Seal and the Crack — Mohenjo-daro Seal DK5175/143, Shang Oracle Bone Ping 0368 & What Ritual Surfaces Preserve
item.description: Comparative material epistemology of ancient religion: what an undeciphered Mohenjo-daro steatite stamp seal (DK5175/143) vs. a dated Late Shang pyro-osteomantic turtle plastron inscription (Ping 0368) can and cannot prove about supernatural agency and ritual rules.

item.title: When the Metronome Stops — Behavioral Synchrony vs. Shared Intentionality, Fire-Walking Heart-Rate Coupling & Public-Goods Triads
item.description: Experimental dissection of collective ritual mechanics: Reddish, Fischer & Bulbulia's (2013) n = 82 triad foot-pedal experiments separating passive metronome synchrony from mutually adjusted shared intentionality, alongside Konvalinka et al.'s fire-walking heart-rate recurrence plots.

item.title: The Water Temple's Calendar — Balinese Subak Irrigation Networks, Lansing & Kremer's Pest-vs.-Water Tradeoff Models & Green Revolution Disruption
item.description: Systems ecology and historical ethnography of Balinese water temples (Lansing 1987, Lansing & Kremer 1993): how ritual cropping calendars balance upstream water scarcity against synchronized fallow pest control, what the 1970s Green Revolution natural experiment revealed, and critiques from historical archival records.

item.title: The Walls That Made Room for a Crowd — Göbekli Tepe Monumental Enclosures vs. Domestic Settlement (Clare 2024) & Massive Basalt Grinding-Stone Work Feasts (Dietrich 2019–2020)
item.description: Archaeological and cooperative architecture of Göbekli Tepe (9600–8000 BCE): Lee Clare's (2024) revised stratigraphic synthesis integrating domestic habitation and water-harvesting infrastructure with monumental T-pillar enclosures, and Laura Dietrich et al.'s (2019, 2020) lithic use-wear and experimental brewing/grinding analysis of thousands of basalt querns and limestone troughs.

item.title: The Stranger in the Sharing Game — Cross-Cultural Random Allocation Games, Moralizing Gods & Impartial Rule Following
item.description: Methodological and statistical audit of cross-cultural Random Allocation Games (Purzycki et al.): how die-roll coin allocations measure impartial rule-following toward distant co-religionists and what the binomial model can and cannot prove.

item.title: What the Ritual Cost — Extreme Rituals, Pain, Heart-Rate Synchrony & Prosocial Donation Experiments
item.description: Field experiments on high-ordeal vs. low-ordeal religious rituals (Xygalatas et al.; Konvalinka et al.): physiological arousal, pain ratings, spectator-performer heart-rate coupling, and anonymous charitable donations.

item.title: What the Neighbors Could See — Credibility Enhancing Displays (CREDs), Public Ritual Observability & Cooperative Trust
item.description: Empirical and evolutionary analysis of observable religious behavior: how public ritual attendance, visible taboos, and Credibility Enhancing Displays (CREDs) solve the cultural transmission problem and shape inter-personal trust among neighbors.

item.title: The Feast in the Ground — Durrington Walls Near Stonehenge (~2500 BCE), Roasted Pig Bones vs. Dairy/Beef Grooved-Ware Lipids, Multi-Isotope Livestock Mobility & Coprolite Parasites
item.description: Multi-proxy archaeological forensics at Durrington Walls (~2500 BCE): resolving the pig-bone vs. cattle/dairy potsherd lipid paradox through culinary segregation (Craig et al. 2015), five-isotope British livestock provenance (Madgwick et al. 2019), and Mitchell's coprolite paleoparasitology showing poorly cooked bovine/canid-shared tapeworm and capillariid infections.

item.title: The Eyes on the Wall — Bateson's Honesty-Box Coffee Experiment, Watching-Eyes Meta-Analyses & Replication Boundaries
item.description: Critical audit of the watching-eyes literature from Bateson et al. (2006) breakroom coffee honesty-box study to large-sample preregistered replications and meta-analyses.

item.title: The Commune That Outlasted Its Neighbors — 19th-Century Religious vs. Secular Communes, Costly Requirements & Survival Hazard Models
item.description: Quantitative survival analysis of 200 nineteenth-century U.S. communes (Sosis & Bressler 2003): how costly taboos and behavioral restrictions correlate with commune longevity differently in religious versus secular communities.

item.title: Who Knew What Was in the Box — Epistemic Access, Secret Ritual Objects, Theory-of-Mind Asymmetries & Religious Authority
item.description: Cognitive and anthropological analysis of hidden ritual contents, asymmetrical epistemic access, and how experiments separate ordinary human false-belief reasoning from attributions of supernatural omniscience.

item.title: The Blank Cell in the Big Gods Debate — Seshat Missing-Data Coding, Chronological Priors & Retraction Reanalysis
item.description: Epistemological and statistical dissection of the Seshat Big Gods controversy: how coding unknown historical cells as zeros shifted the inferred appearance of moralizing gods relative to social complexity, and why absence of evidence, documented absence, and first attestation are distinct.

item.title: The Preservative That Raised a Hormone — Oral Calcium Propionate Crossover Trials (Tirosh 2019 n=14 & Adler 2021 Clamps n=28), Glucagon/FABP4/Norepinephrine Signals & [6,6-2H2]Glucose Endogenous Flux
item.description: Dissecting acute human metabolic responses to oral calcium propionate vs. colonic fermentation (Boets 9.2% systemic appearance): Tirosh et al.'s (2019) 14-volunteer mixed-meal crossover showing postprandial rises in norepinephrine, glucagon, and FABP4, paired with Adler et al.'s (2021) [6,6-2H2]glucose tracer clamp crossover across fasting rest, euglycemia, and mild hypoglycemia.

item.title: The Glucose That Couldn't Leave the Liver — Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia, ER G6PC1 His176 Phosphohistidine Catalysis vs. SLC37A4, Uncooked Cornstarch & DTX401 Gene Therapy
item.description: From acute fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis in glycogen storage disease type Ia to ER lumenal G6PC1 His176 phosphohistidine hydrolysis vs. SLC37A4 glucose-6-phosphate transport, Grefhorst's ChREBP/LXRalpha mouse blockade vs. human [6,6-2H2]glucose flux, uncooked cornstarch therapy, and AAV8 G6PC1 gene replacement.

item.title: The Bile Acid That Missed the Return Trip — Ileal ASBT Reclamation, FXR–FGF19–CYP7A1 Feedback (6HL1), 75SeHCAT Retention, Serum C4 & SINBAD Trial
item.description: Enterohepatic circulation and bile acid malabsorption: apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter (ASBT/SLC10A2), human FXR ligand-binding domain (PDB 6HL1), ileal FGF19 suppression of hepatic CYP7A1, 7-day 75SeHCAT gamma retention vs. fasting serum 7alpha-hydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one (C4), and colesevelam sequestration in the SINBAD trial.

item.title: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon
item.description: Archaeotoxicology and receptor pharmacology of ancient cannabis at Tunnug 1 (Tuva, Early Iron Age): LC-HRMS/MS detection of cannabinol (CBN) in a preserved human hair braid alongside 965 botanical cannabis seeds, Hallstatt Plateau 14C calibration, human CB1-Gi1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 9ERX), forensic hair-testing boundaries between smoke/handling transfer and metabolic THC-COOH incorporation (Moosmann et al. 2015), and comparative Eurasian archaeobotany.

item.title: The Floor That Kept the Dead — Neolithic Çatalhöyük Subfloor Burials (Haddow 2025), Shifting Intra-Building Genetic Kinship Across 1,000 Years (63% to 22%, Yaka 2021 & Yüncü 2025) & Maternal Lineage Ties
item.description: Stratigraphic bioarchaeology and ancient DNA of subfloor house burials across Neolithic Anatolia: Haddow et al.'s (2025) house-life-cycle burial patterns at Çatalhöyük (including Building 42's foundation burial), Yaka et al.'s (2021) transition from biological kin burials at Aşıklı Höyük/Boncuklu to co-burial of unrelated individuals, and Yüncü et al.'s (2025) 131-genome time series revealing declining intra-building genetic kinship (63% -> 30% -> 22%), maternal house linkages, and female subadult grave goods.

item.title: The Foot That Healed — 31,000-Year-Old Borneo Distal Lower-Leg Amputation, Cortical Remodeling & Pleistocene Surgical Care
item.description: Osteoarchaeological and paleopathological analysis of the 31,000-year-old Liang Tebo burial in Borneo (Maloney et al. 2022): healed distal tibia and fibula amputation with 6–9 years of post-operative survival and absence of osteomyelitis.

item.title: The Ground Had a Second Story — Clandestine Burials, Taphonomy & Soil Forensics
item.description: Behind the Curtain Evidence Ledger & Longform Analysis (The Ground Had a Second Story): specimen-bound diagnostic mechanics, assay boundaries, and real clinical/forensic case studies.

item.title: Settling Red Cells & the 100,000-Colony Myth — ESR vs. CRP Kinetics, Procalcitonin Stewardship & Urine Culture Across Species
item.description: One Medicine inflammatory & microbiology deep dive (H013, H017, V010, V001, V002): Westergren ESR zeta-potential dissipation & fibrinogen rouleaux physics vs. equine physiological rouleaux & feline/canine Serum Amyloid A (SAA)/CRP kinetics, hepatic CRP 19-hour constant half-life, ESR/CRP discordance in SLE & giant cell arteritis, Procalcitonin (PCT) antibiotic stewardship & non-infectious surges, paired with Edward Kass's 10^5 CFU/mL pyelonephritis threshold misapplied to acute dysuria (Stamm 10^2 CFU/mL), veterinary ultrasound-guided cystocentesis vs. voided contamination, and why treating asymptomatic/subclinical bacteriuria in humans, dogs, and cats breeds multidrug resistance.

item.title: Shadows, Acoustic Windows & Operator Hands — Two-View Veterinary Radiography, Ultrasound Artifacts, Twisted Stomachs & Missing Stones
item.description: One Medicine diagnostic imaging deep dive (V013, V014, H005, H032): 5 radiographic opacities & 3-view thoracic gravity physics, ICRP/ACVR collimation vs. digital cropping eye-lens scatter, AI dataset shift traps, pulmonary metastasis CT vs. X-ray size thresholds, counterclockwise canine GDV missed as sand impaction, Vizsla shotgun survival vs. Cane Corso forensic necropsy, Hermann's tortoise retained egg, paired with B-mode ultrasound physics, AFAST fluid scores vs. centesis, feline moth-eaten spleen & canine cavitated splenic hemangiosarcoma myths (42% Se / 51% Sp), feline ureteroliths, liver biopsy PCV drops, and equine colic FLASH.

item.title: The Grave With Two Calendars — Repton Viking Charnel Deposit, Anglo-Saxon Silver Coin Hoard (873–874 CE) vs. Bone Collagen Radiocarbon & Marine Reservoir Correction
item.description: Archaeometric resolution of the Repton Viking Great Army charnel deposit: why five silver pennies in Grave 529 dated the burial to 873–874 CE while uncalibrated terrestrial bone collagen 14C dates appeared centuries older, and how Jarman et al. (2018) combined delta-13C/delta-15N dietary paleodiet reconstruction with marine reservoir correction (Heaton et al. 2020 Marine20) to reconcile the numismatic and radiocarbon calendars.

item.title: The Dogs Before the Map — Lawyer's Cave Coastal Alaska Femur, Koster & Stilwell II Intentional Dog Burials (~10,000 BP), Swan Point & Beringian Canids & Pre-Contact Indigenous American Dog Genomes
item.description: Zooarchaeology, radiocarbon reservoir effects, and paleogenomics of early dogs in the Americas: da Silva Coelho et al. (2021) Lawyer's Cave southeast Alaska femur fragment and marine dietary offset, Perri et al.'s directly dated Koster and Stilwell II Illinois dog burials (~10,190-9,630 cal BP), Lanoë et al. (2024) Swan Point subarctic salmon-fed canids, Graf et al. (2026) Beringian base camp, and Ní Leathlobhair et al. (2018) pre-contact American dog clade.

item.title: Alkaline Lithium Springs & Unchained Asylums — Soranus of Ephesus & Humane Roman Psychiatry
item.description: How Soranus of Ephesus (~100 CE) condemned chains, darkness, and the 'wandering womb' myth while prescribing cognitive rehabilitation and lithium-rich alkaline waters.

item.title: Dream Surgery at Epidaurus — Asclepian Sleep Temples, Sacred Snakes & Placebo Neurobiology
item.description: Walks into the 4th-century BCE abaton at Epidaurus—translating the carved Iamata stelae alongside archaeological scalpels and modern PAG opioid/CB1 imaging.

item.title: Babylonian Neurology vs. Cos — Esagil-kin-apli's 1050 BCE Seizure Tablet & Hippocrates
item.description: Reads Neo-Babylonian Sakikkū Tablet XXVI (~1050 BCE) side-by-side with Hippocrates's On the Sacred Disease (~400 BCE): Jacksonian marches, auras, and post-ictal paresis.
